intended_object: The real-part projection x + i·y ↦ x from the complexification H_ℂ of a real inner product space H back to H, as a bounded (norm ≤ 1) ℝ-linear map. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The library defines `Complexification H` as `H × H`, where the pair (x, y) stands for x + i·y. `fstL` takes the ℝ-linear map `fstₗ : u ↦ u.1`, which is linear because addition and real scalar multiplication act componentwise (`add_fst`, `rsmul_fst`). It then makes the map continuous with `mkContinuous`, using the bound ‖u.1‖ ≤ 1·‖u‖ (`norm_fst_le`, which follows from ‖u‖² = ‖u.1‖² + ‖u.2‖²). This is exactly the real-part projection, as a continuous ℝ-linear map, with norm at most 1.

The map belongs to the library's own `Complexification` type. Mathlib has no complexification of a real inner product space carrying its complex inner product, so there is nothing more general to compare it with. The real-inner-product-space setting is the one the construction is built in. The definition is therefore neither narrower than needed nor incorrect.
